subject.title: Feature: configurable bootstrap file injection order for prompt cache optimization

question: Should OpenClaw add a core configuration/API surface for dynamic bootstrap file classification and prompt order, or route this through the existing context-engine/plugin/bootstrap-hook model instead?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix would create public prompt-cache and config semantics in an area where repository policy sets a high bar for new knobs and long-term compatibility.

options.title: Add a narrow core/context contract
options.body: Define one documented dynamic-file/order surface with default-compatible behavior, config schema/help/docs, and tests proving stable versus dynamic prompt placement.

options.title: Use existing extension hooks
options.body: Document an operator-supported `agent:bootstrap` or context-engine path instead of adding new core config keys, and keep the core runtime lean.

options.title: Defer to broader cacheWrite work
options.body: Keep this blocked behind the wider session-freeze/cacheWrite spiral decision tracked by related issues before adding any new surface.

recommendation.title: Add a narrow core/context contract
recommendation.body: Define one documented dynamic-file/order surface with default-compatible behavior, config schema/help/docs, and tests proving stable versus dynamic prompt placement.

likelyOwner.reason: Current prompt/config blame and broader system-prompt history make this the best available owner for the product/API shape decision.
